many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only

entry = rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC task-ae1e7c68: connect axis-aligned diamond centers', id='arc_task_ae1e7c68_connect_aligned_diamond_centers', path='arc-patterns', global_=True, content='For ARC task-ae1e7c68, the foreground 2 objects are hollow 4-point diamonds: four pixels at the cardinal neighbors of an absent center, in a 3x3 footprint. First identify EVERY such diamond (do not miss an object simply because its pixels are near another diamond). For every pair of diamond centers sharing a row or column, connect them in that row/column with color 1, filling only the gap between their nearest facing diamond pixels; keep all original 2s and other background unchanged. No diagonal connections. If several diamonds share a row/column, connect the sequence across gaps. Confirmed demos: (a) centers (1,3),(1,10),(5,10) connect along row 1 between first two and col 10 between next pair. (b) centers (3,3),(3,8),(3,13),(10,2),(9,8): connect the three row-3 diamonds and connect centers (3,8) to (9,8), leaving unaligned bottom-left diamond unconnected. (c) centers (1,8),(4,4),(4,11),(9,4),(9,11): connect horizontal pairs in rows 4 and 9 and vertical pairs in cols 4 and 11; leave lone center (1,8) unconnected. Accepted test centers were (2,2),(4,7),(6,2),(6,10). Connect (2,2) to (6,2) with 1 at (4,2), and connect (6,2) to (6,10) with 1 at row 6, cols 4–8. Crucial: there are FOUR diamonds in that test; the pair centered (6,2) and (6,10) is easily overlooked. Wrong guesses were (i) connecting pairs whose outer tips happen to share a row, even though centers are not aligned, and (ii) leaving the grid unchanged after missing the fourth diamond. The rule is alignment of diamond CENTERS, not arbitrary aligned tip endpoints. Output connector color is 1 regardless of original background 0 and diamond color 2.')
